note: Combined sales-tax rates from state or city revenue departments. Applied to the food estimate unless a venue prints its own percent. The site rental is taxed only when that venue's price list says so. Service-charge taxability is left unknown unless the official page says the charge is taxable.

FL-ORANGE.name: Orange County, Florida
FL-ORANGE.quote: Florida's general state sales tax rate is 6%. Form DR-15DSS for 2026 lists Orange County discretionary surtax at .5% (Jan 1, 2003 through Dec 31, 2035). Combined 6.5%.
FL-ORANGE.note: Estimated from the official local rate: Florida's 6% state sales tax plus Orange County's 0.5% discretionary surtax on Form DR-15DSS. Applied to the food line. The rental is taxed only when the venue prints a tax percent.

FL-MIAMI-DADE.name: Miami-Dade County, Florida
FL-MIAMI-DADE.quote: Florida's general state sales tax rate is 6%. Form DR-15DSS for 2026 lists Miami-Dade discretionary surtax at 1% (Jan 1, 1992). Combined 7%.
FL-MIAMI-DADE.note: Estimated from the official local rate: Florida 6% plus Miami-Dade's 1% surtax. Applied to the food line.

FL-HILLSBOROUGH.name: Hillsborough County, Florida
FL-HILLSBOROUGH.quote: Florida's general state sales tax rate is 6%. Form DR-15DSS for 2026 lists Hillsborough discretionary surtax at 1.5%. Combined 7.5%.
FL-HILLSBOROUGH.note: Estimated from the official local rate: Florida 6% plus Hillsborough County's 1.5% surtax. Applied to the food line.

FL-PINELLAS.name: Pinellas County, Florida
FL-PINELLAS.quote: Florida's general state sales tax rate is 6%. Form DR-15DSS for 2026 lists Pinellas discretionary surtax at 1% (Feb 1, 1990 through Dec 31, 2029). Combined 7%.
FL-PINELLAS.note: Estimated from the official local rate: Florida 6% plus Pinellas County's 1% surtax. Applied to the food line.

TX-DALLAS.name: Dallas, Texas
TX-DALLAS.quote: Dallas (Dallas Co), local code 2057011, local rate .010000, total rate .082500, plus Dallas MTA .010000.
TX-DALLAS.note: Estimated from the Texas Comptroller city table. The total-rate column is 8.25% for Dallas in Dallas County. Applied to the food line.

TX-FORTWORTH.name: Fort Worth, Texas
TX-FORTWORTH.quote: Fort Worth (Tarrant Co), local code 2220031, local rate .010000, total rate .082500.
TX-FORTWORTH.note: Estimated from the Texas Comptroller city table. Total rate 8.25% for Fort Worth in Tarrant County. Applied to the food line.

TX-HOUSTON.name: Houston, Texas
TX-HOUSTON.quote: Houston (Harris Co), local code 2101017, local rate .010000, total rate .082500, plus Houston MTA .010000.
TX-HOUSTON.note: Estimated from the Texas Comptroller city table. Total rate 8.25% for Houston in Harris County on the row that includes Houston MTA. Some emergency-services districts inside the city are listed separately and can change the local split, still under the 8.25% combined cap shown on those rows. Applied to the food line.

TX-AUSTIN.name: Austin, Texas
TX-AUSTIN.quote: Austin (Travis Co), local code 2227016, local rate .010000, total rate .082500, plus Austin MTA .010000.
TX-AUSTIN.note: Estimated from the Texas Comptroller city table. Total rate 8.25% for Austin in Travis County. Applied to the food line.

TX-SANANTONIO.name: San Antonio, Texas
TX-SANANTONIO.quote: San Antonio (Bexar Co), local code 2015012, local rate .011250, total rate .082500, plus San Antonio ATD .003750 and San Antonio MTA .005000.
TX-SANANTONIO.note: Estimated from the Texas Comptroller city table. Total rate 8.25% for San Antonio in Bexar County. Applied to the food line.

CA-LOSANGELES.name: Los Angeles and Beverly Hills, California
CA-LOSANGELES.quote: California City & County Sales & Use Tax Rates, effective October 1, 2026: Los Angeles 10.250% and Beverly Hills 10.250%.
CA-LOSANGELES.note: Estimated from the CDTFA city rate effective October 1, 2026. Applied to the food line. Other Los Angeles County cities on that table are higher, so this rate is not used outside Los Angeles and Beverly Hills.

CA-SANFRANCISCO.name: San Francisco, California
CA-SANFRANCISCO.quote: California City & County Sales & Use Tax Rates, effective October 1, 2026: San Francisco 8.625%.
CA-SANFRANCISCO.note: Estimated from the CDTFA city rate effective October 1, 2026. Applied to the food line.

CA-SANDIEGO.name: San Diego, California
CA-SANDIEGO.quote: California City & County Sales & Use Tax Rates, effective October 1, 2026: San Diego 7.750%.
CA-SANDIEGO.note: Estimated from the CDTFA city rate effective October 1, 2026. Applied to the food line. Nearby cities such as Del Mar are a different rate and are not given this one.

IL-CHICAGO.name: Chicago, Illinois
IL-CHICAGO.quote: Illinois Department of Revenue PIO-114, Example 1, General Merchandise, City of Chicago (Cook County): state tax total 6.25% + RTA 1.00% + Chicago home rule 1.25% + Cook County home rule 1.75% = 10.25%. Chicago restaurant tax, Municipal Code 3-30, is 0.50% as of 1/1/2020.
IL-CHICAGO.note: Estimated from the official rates. Prepared food uses Illinois' general-merchandise rate. Chicago's 0.50% restaurant tax is added. The 1% MPEA food-and-beverage tax applies only in a downtown district and at the airports, so it is not in this 10.75% citywide figure. Applied to the food line.
IL-CHICAGO.review: Confirm whether a specific venue sits inside the MPEA district. That adds 1% and is not in this rate.

WA-SEATTLE.name: Seattle, Washington
WA-SEATTLE.quote: Washington Department of Revenue local sales and use tax rates, October 1 through December 31, 2026: King Seattle, location code 1726, local .0405, state .0650, combined .1055. Combined sales tax includes the 6.5% state rate and the local rate.
WA-SEATTLE.note: Estimated from the Department of Revenue quarterly rate table. 10.55% applied to the food line. Snoqualmie is a different location code and is not given this rate.

NY-NYC.name: New York City
NY-NYC.quote: NYC Department of Finance: food and beverages sold by restaurants and caterers are taxed at a total sales and use tax of 8.875 percent (city 4.5%, state 4%, MCTD 0.375%). Tax Bulletin TB-ST-806: separately stated service charges or other charges not specifically listed as gratuities on a bill or invoice are subject to sales tax.
NY-NYC.note: Estimated from the city's 8.875% rate for restaurant and caterer food and beverages. The same percent is also applied to the service-charge line, because TB-ST-806 says a service charge that is not identified as a gratuity is taxable. A charge that is separately stated, called a gratuity, and paid entirely to employees is not given this treatment.

OR-STATE.name: Oregon
OR-STATE.quote: Oregon doesn't have a general sales or use/transaction tax.
OR-STATE.note: Oregon Department of Revenue: no general sales tax. The tax line is $0. This is not a guessed rate. Oregon does tax some vehicle purchases, which is not a wedding meal.

GA-ATLANTA.name: Atlanta, Georgia
GA-ATLANTA.quote: Georgia Department of Revenue general rate chart effective October 1, 2026: Fulton (Atlanta) 8.9 and DeKalb (Atlanta) 8.9. The chart says the 4% state rate is included.
GA-ATLANTA.note: Estimated from the October 1, 2026 Georgia rate chart for the City of Atlanta in Fulton and DeKalb. Applied to the food line. Roswell and other suburbs are not given this rate.

MN-MINNEAPOLIS.name: Minneapolis, Minnesota
MN-MINNEAPOLIS.quote: Minnesota Department of Revenue local sales and use tax rate guide, 2026 Q4: Minneapolis total 9.025% (state 6.875%). The guide says the table does not include special local taxes such as restaurant tax.
MN-MINNEAPOLIS.note: Estimated from the general Minneapolis sales-tax rate of 9.025%. The Department's Q4 metro guide says this table does not include special local restaurant taxes, and those extra rates are not added here.
MN-MINNEAPOLIS.review: Fact Sheet 164M (revised February 2025) adds a 3% downtown restaurant tax, and its combination table shows 12.025% for a downtown restaurant with no live entertainment. The same sheet says service charges in a lodging facility's meeting or banquet room are subject to the Minneapolis restaurant taxes. That downtown rate and that service-charge rule are not applied to every Minneapolis venue.

LA-NEWORLEANS.name: New Orleans, Louisiana
LA-NEWORLEANS.quote: Louisiana Department of Revenue: the state sales tax rate is 5%. City of New Orleans sales-tax form instructions refer to the City of New Orleans 5% sales tax on taxable goods.
LA-NEWORLEANS.note: Estimated from the City of New Orleans page stating the combined Louisiana and Orleans Parish rate is 10% for sales of tangible personal property. The same page lists a 4.5% food-and-drug rate and does not say restaurant meals use that column, so 4.5% is not applied. It also lists extra district rates, including the French Quarter economic development district.
LA-NEWORLEANS.review: Confirm the venue is not inside a New Orleans special taxing district with a higher local rate.

TN-DAVIDSON.name: Nashville and Davidson County, Tennessee
TN-DAVIDSON.quote: Tennessee Department of Revenue notice: Davidson County's local sales tax rate increased to 2.75% effective February 1, 2025. The Department's sales-tax chart states the state rate as 7.0%. Combined 9.75%.
TN-DAVIDSON.note: Estimated for prepared food: Important Notice 17-21 says prepared food is taxed at the 7% state rate plus the local rate, and that the 4% food rate does not include prepared food. Davidson County's local rate on the Department's rate map, including the transit surcharge, is 2.75%. Combined 9.75% on the food line.
TN-DAVIDSON.review: Notice 26-19, dated September 2026, says other tangible personal property remains at a 2.25% Davidson local rate, and that grocery food drops to 1.75% local on November 1, 2026. Prepared food is excluded from that grocery cut. Reconcile the 2.25% sentence with the 2.75% surcharge on the rate map.

DC-WASHINGTON.name: Washington, District of Columbia
DC-WASHINGTON.quote: Food and Beverage Tax: Sales of food or drink served or prepared for immediate consumption, or sold in or by restaurants, lunch counters, cafeterias, hotels, snack bars, caterers, boarding houses, carry-out shops and like places of business, are subject to tax at the rate of 10%. The 2026 FR-800 instructions repeat that 10% rate for food and drink for immediate consumption.
DC-WASHINGTON.note: Estimated from the District's 10% food-and-beverage rate on catered and restaurant meals. Applied to the food line. The CFO rates page lists the general tangible-property rate at 6.0% through September 30, 2027, and lists restaurant meals at 10%. The general rate is not used here. Vienna, Virginia is not in the District.
DC-WASHINGTON.review: OTR noted a temporary change to the general sales-tax rate. The 2026 return instructions still state 10% for food and drink for immediate consumption. Re-check that the meals line was not retitled.

PA-PHILADELPHIA.name: Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
PA-PHILADELPHIA.quote: Philadelphia's combined sales tax rate is 8%: 6% Pennsylvania sales tax, plus 2% Philadelphia sales tax. This rate won't change. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue restaurant guide says sales of food and non-alcoholic beverages by a caterer or eating establishment are taxable, with an additional 2% in Philadelphia.
PA-PHILADELPHIA.note: Estimated from the City of Philadelphia's stated 8% combined rate on taxable sales, which includes catered food. Applied to the food line. Winterthur is in Delaware and is not given this rate. Act 21 of 2026 changes where the 2% local tax is sourced; the city says the rate itself stays 8%.

CO-DENVER-FOOD.name: Denver, Colorado, prepared food and drink
CO-DENVER-FOOD.quote: Denver Treasury combined rate for Prepared Food and Drink: Denver 4.00%, State 2.90%, RTD 1.00%, special district 0.10%, total 8.00%. The general sales rate on the same table is 9.15% and is not used for the food line.
CO-DENVER-FOOD.note: Estimated from Denver's prepared-food-and-drink column, not the general 9.15% sales rate. Applied to the food line. Golden and Littleton are separate home-rule cities and are not given Denver's rate.

AZ-PHOENIX-RESTAURANT.name: Phoenix, Arizona, restaurants and bars
AZ-PHOENIX-RESTAURANT.quote: City of Phoenix combined tax-rate chart effective January 1, 2026: Restaurants and Bars, business code 011, Phoenix 2.800%, state 5.600%, county 0.700%, combined 9.100%.
AZ-PHOENIX-RESTAURANT.note: Estimated from the city's restaurants-and-bars row. Applied to the food line. Paradise Valley publishes its own city rate and is not given Phoenix's combined rate. Retail sales use a two-level structure that does not apply to this restaurant row.

NV-CLARK.name: Clark County, Nevada
NV-CLARK.quote: Nevada Department of Taxation: Effective January 1, 2020 the Clark County Sales and Use Tax rate increased to 8.375%. The Clark County rate sheet is listed as effective 1/1/2020.
NV-CLARK.note: Estimated from the Department's Clark County combined rate of 8.375%. Applied to the food line. The rate sheet says it is for reference and points to NRS 360.299 for the calculation rules.

SC-CHARLESTON.name: Charleston County, South Carolina
SC-CHARLESTON.quote: South Carolina Department of Revenue form ST-500, effective May 1, 2026: Charleston 9%, local taxes LO, TT, and ECI. The statewide rate is 6%, and the local chart adds the county taxes collected by the Department.
SC-CHARLESTON.note: Estimated from SCDOR's 9% combined rate for Charleston County. Applied to the food line. ST-500 says it does not include local taxes that counties or municipalities collect themselves.
SC-CHARLESTON.review: A city hospitality tax on prepared meals, if Charleston still levies one, is collected outside this SCDOR chart and is not included.

MA-MEALS.name: Massachusetts state meals tax
MA-MEALS.quote: Massachusetts imposes a sales tax on meals sold by restaurants. The tax is 6.25% of the sales price of the meal. A city or town may add a 0.75% local option meals excise.
MA-MEALS.note: Estimated from the 6.25% state meals tax only. Applied to the food line, including Boston. The 0.75% local option is omitted because no Department of Revenue adoption list opened for this check names the city or town.
MA-MEALS.review: If a DOR adoption list shows this city has accepted the 0.75% local meals excise, the meals total is 7%. A meals-and-rooms distribution report is not that list, because it also includes room tax.

NC-MECKLENBURG.name: Mecklenburg County, North Carolina
NC-MECKLENBURG.quote: NCDOR: effective July 1, 2026, Mecklenburg County's general rate is 8.25% (county 2.00%, transit 0.50%, additional county 1.00%, state 4.75%). Prepared food is non-qualifying food, so the general state and local rates apply. Qualifying groceries stay at 2%.
NC-MECKLENBURG.note: Estimated from NCDOR's 8.25% general rate, which applies to prepared food. Applied to the food line. The current-rates page says these rates do not include prepared-meal taxes that local governments administer themselves.
NC-MECKLENBURG.review: Charlotte's separately administered prepared-meal tax, if still in force, is not in the NCDOR 8.25% figure. The Mint Museum brochures already print 8.25% on drink prices.
